note: jwt_path_auth adds a global authentication provider (id jwt_path_auth) that reads a JWT from the ?jwt= query string, but only for request paths beginning with one of jwt_path_auth.config -> allowed_path_prefixes (config/install default ['/system/files/']). The token must carry drupal.path_auth.uid and drupal.path_auth.path claims. Config form route jwt_path_auth.config_form at /admin/config/system/jwt/path-auth (permission 'administer jwt'). Medium/hard cases are grounded entirely in the real allowed_path_prefixes config (never jwt.config): mediums read a known prefix list, hards add/replace prefixes and verify the live list.

evals.prompt: How does the Drupal jwt_path_auth module expect a JWT to be supplied on a request, and what limits where that is accepted?
evals.expected_output: The token is passed in the ?jwt= query-string parameter. The provider only applies when the request path starts with one of the configured jwt_path_auth.config allowed_path_prefixes (default /system/files/).

evals.prompt: Out of the box, on which path(s) does jwt_path_auth accept a query-string JWT, and where do you change that?
evals.expected_output: The shipped default allowed_path_prefixes is ['/system/files/'] (private files). Change it in jwt_path_auth.config, via the form at /admin/config/system/jwt/path-auth (route jwt_path_auth.config_form, permission 'administer jwt').

evals.prompt: Which claims must a token carry for jwt_path_auth to authenticate a request, and how is the token bound to a specific URL?
evals.expected_output: The token must include nested claims drupal.path_auth.uid and drupal.path_auth.path. Authentication succeeds only if the request path starts with the token's path claim, binding the token to a URL prefix.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which request-path prefixes will jwt_path_auth accept a query-string JWT on? Inspect the live configuration and list them.
evals.expected_output: allowed_path_prefixes is ['/jwtpa-eval/', '/system/files/'] on this site. Read it with `drush cget jwt_path_auth.config allowed_path_prefixes`.

evals.prompt: A JWT is passed as ?jwt=... on this site. Inspect the live jwt_path_auth configuration and state the single path prefix under which such a token would be accepted.
evals.expected_output: allowed_path_prefixes is ['/jwtpa-report/']. Only requests whose path begins with /jwtpa-report/ will attempt query-string JWT auth. Read it with `drush cget jwt_path_auth.config allowed_path_prefixes`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, query-string JWT authentication should also work for URLs under /jwtpa-task/, in addition to whatever is already allowed. Update jwt_path_auth so that /jwtpa-task/ is an accepted path prefix. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add '/jwtpa-task/' to jwt_path_auth.config allowed_path_prefixes (via the path-auth config form or config). Verify passes when '/jwtpa-task/' is present in the list.

evals.prompt: This site should accept query-string JWTs ONLY on URLs under /downloads/ — no other paths, including the default private-files path. Configure jwt_path_auth so its allowed path prefixes are exactly ['/downloads/']. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set jwt_path_auth.config allowed_path_prefixes to exactly ['/downloads/'] (replacing the default). Verify passes when the list equals ['/downloads/'].
